lifecycle.create: MemoryEngine.create writes provenance with the id (owner, conversation, session, scope, source, confidence)
lifecycle.correction: supersede() records history and advances updatedAt strictly monotonically, so same-millisecond corrections still order correctly
lifecycle.reinforce: same fact again strengthens confidence and advances updatedAt; the ORIGIN never moves
lifecycle.conversation_delete: GenesisCore.closeConversation → MultiChatStore.remove + AIService.forgetConversation → session memories and that conversation's graph nodes
lifecycle.retention: durable facts survive conversation deletion with their origin intact; session material does not
lifecycle.session_expiry: session-scoped records are rejected outside their session (M22 test A)

propagation.semantic_index: none — PatternMemory is the one index; there is no second vector store to drift
propagation.cognitive_graph: nodes linked by memoryId are purged; edges touching them are removed
propagation.project_summaries: project notes are independent user content and are not edited by memory deletion
propagation.agent_context: agent requests read through the same store, so a deleted memory cannot reappear there
propagation.background_processes: curiosity/self-study use the same scoped recall

evidence: test K: deleting a memory removes its cognitive observation too
test K: deleting a conversation purges its session material, keeps durable facts
test K: state() refuses unattributed observations and other conversations' nodes

conversation_delete_keeps: persistent-user facts, still labelled with the deleted chat as their origin
policy.why: the mission forbids making LÉLU forget the user; deleting a chat is not "forget everything you know about me"

residual_risks: Ordinary turn memories are stored as persistent-user by MemoryEngine, so they survive their chat. This is the documented product policy, not a leak: they are recallable only as labelled history.
Project notes that quoted a memory are not rewritten when that memory is deleted.
